an AdapPID control system for an EVCS is proposed and validated in this paper.
the proposed energy management system of the charging station is able to provide an optimal charging and discharging solution for the charging station and the hybrid power system.

the development of a novel control strategy that can be used to manage energy flows in the charging station and the grid-connected hybrid power systems.
the energy management system of a grid-connected hybrid system and the charging station which has been integrated into the hybrid system.
energy management of the CS, and its contribution is the development of a control scheme to manage the energy of a CS in a grid-connected system.

the proposed energy management system is able to provide the charging and discharging services of PHEVs in a grid-connected renewable hybrid power system.
the proposed AdapPID control scheme has been shown to provide an efficient, reliable and robust energy management and control of a CS.
the AdapPID controller is more effective than the conventional PID controller in terms of settling time, overshoot and steady state error for the charging and discharging processes of the CS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed energy management system and control scheme is able to control the power flows of all the subsystems and charging/discharging of the vehicles simultaneously to fulfil the charging and discharging needs of all the vehicles in a CS.

, the AdapPID controller has the ability to control the charging and discharging processes of the CS with a high level of accuracy and stability, and also the AdapPID controlled CS is capable to provide a high quality power supply to the grid and the vehicles.
the developed AdapPID controller has the ability to provide the required power to the CS and the storage system with a fast and robust response to the load and renewable energy sources variations.

, a charging station with the proposed control strategy can effectively manage and control the charging and discharging process of five PHEVs and the renewable energy sources to satisfy the grid requirements and the charging and dis-charging demands of PHEVs.
